The footnote problem in technical writing

Footnotes are a venerable convention in academic writing, but in HTML they are routinely stripped or re-rooted to the end of the document.1 When extracting the body, we need to either keep them inline or rebuild a sensible footnote section.

Why this matters

Reader experience degrades when footnotes are silently dropped or duplicated into the body as parentheticals.

Our approach

We preserve footnote references inline during extraction and emit a final footnotes section, separated by a horizontal rule.
